title: dumpex v2 structured output (schema_version 2.18)
description: Validates the v2.18 `--json` envelope for --list, --modules, --threads, --process, --sysinfo, --handles, --profile, --diff, --extract, --strings, --report, and --hunt. `result.kind` selects the record and summary shapes. Record objects are closed where declared; `processRecord.peb_extended` is the only optional record property and appears only for `--process --verbose`. Hunt investigation actions are present only for `selected == "all"` and describe unresolved coverage targets rather than verdicts. Later same-version addition (still schema_version 2.13): `coverageLimitation.code` may be `SCAN_ITEMS_UNACCOUNTED` -- N region(s) or segment(s) whose outcome a scan's own eligibility ledger cannot reconcile, either taken into scope with no outcome recorded or an outcome recorded for items never taken into scope. It always emits `targets: []` (an unreconciled item is one whose identity the scan never captured) and carries `affected_count`; `scope` names the scan layer (sleep_mask, entropy, or decode) when `source` is "encoding_scan". The `code` field is open, so this is additive for consumers pinned to 2.13. v2.14 exposes `--hunt-addr` targeted rescans: every `hunt` summary carries a closed `scan_scope` tag naming what the invocation covered, and a targeted result's hunter details additionally carry one `targeted_scope` entry per coverage closure. Full-scope hunt details omit `targeted_scope` entirely rather than emitting null. A `hunt` result's `summary.scan_scope` is cross-checked against the rest of the document: a `targeted` tag pins `summary.selected` to the same analyzer (which in turn pins the single record's `hunter`), pins `source`/`scopes` to that analyzer's registered targeted capability, and requires `targeted_scope` on the record's details; a `full` tag forbids `targeted_scope`. Later same-version addition (still schema_version 2.14, which is unreleased): a `targeted_scope` entry additionally carries `applicability_reason` and `measurements`, and its `coverage_status` may be "not_applicable" -- the source's own descriptor-eligibility gate declined the target, which is the boundary of what that source speaks about rather than a gap in what it did. A consumer must not count "not_applicable" as a coverage failure: the record's `coverage.status` does not, and a rescan whose every closure is inapplicable reports `coverage.status` "not_evaluated". v2.15 adds `coverage.missed_bytes`, required on every result and on every hunter record: how much captured in-scope memory the run's own coverage gaps add up to. `state` labels the figure -- "exact" (every gap's extent is established), "lower_bound" (some gaps could not be measured, so `bytes` is a floor), or "unknown" (no gap's extent is established, and `bytes` is null rather than 0). `complete` is true exactly when `unquantified_gaps` is 0, which is exactly when `state` is "exact". A consumer thresholding on `bytes` must read `state` first: null and a lower bound both mean something other than "this much was missed", and 0 with state "exact" is the only way to say nothing capturable was missed. `bytes` measures MEMORY: it is a union of address ranges, so one physical region named by several gaps at once (obfuscation's three scan layers skip overlapping region sets, and one region can exceed two or three of their caps) is counted once. `quantified_gaps` counts the gap records, `distinct_ranges` the physical ranges they cover once merged, and `distinct_ranges <= quantified_gaps` always; neither counts bytes, and neither does a limitation's own `affected_count`. The same version adds `examined_size` and `unexamined_size` to `scanTarget`: how many of that target's captured bytes a scan actually looked at, and the remainder it did not. Both are null when the extent was never established, which is not the same claim as 0; `unexamined_size` is derived from `captured_size - examined_size`, and the aggregate is the union of exactly those per-target remainders, so the two cannot disagree. `coverage.status` keeps its three values and its meaning: this grades a `partial`, it does not redefine when one is reported. v2.16 adds `eligible_bytes`, `unscanned_pass_bytes` and `unscanned_fraction` to `coverage.missed_bytes`: how much scanning work the run had in front of it, how much of that work did not happen, and the second as a proportion of the first. The proportion is what lets one run be judged on its own -- 3.2 MB unscanned is a rounding error out of 11.4 GB eligible and almost the whole hunt out of 3.4 MB -- so a single threshold can be applied across dumps of any size. Both are measured PER SCAN PASS and summed over the passes, which is a different basis from `bytes`: a hunter running three passes over one region had three passes' worth of work in front of it, and a region only one pass skipped is one pass's worth of work not done. `bytes` keeps its own basis (memory with at least one unanswered question, unioned across passes, what a re-collection would have to recover) and is deliberately NOT the numerator here: dividing it by a per-pass scope would report a region EVERY pass skipped as two-thirds scanned. Within one pass the unexamined ranges are unioned, so a segment reported under two codes at once costs that pass's work once; across passes they are summed. A pass's scope includes items a whole-scan budget left unreached, so every gap it reports is inside the scope it is measured against and `unscanned_pass_bytes <= eligible_bytes` always. The scope is per producer and reflects that producer's own filters, so two hunters over one dump legitimately report different denominators; it is a property of the hunter, never of the dump. `eligible_bytes` and `unscanned_fraction` are null when no denominator was established -- a producer that measures no eligibility, a scan loop that took items into scope without measuring them, and every `coverage.status` of "not_evaluated", which has no work for a gap to be a proportion of. Null and 0 are different answers: 0 says a scan measured its scope and had no capturable memory in front of it. `unscanned_fraction` is additionally null when `state` is "unknown": null is the only honest answer where no gap has a measured extent, and 0 is reserved for a run that missed nothing. Where it is non-null it is exactly `unscanned_pass_bytes / eligible_bytes` and carries `state`'s own qualifier -- an exact proportion when "exact", a floor under the real one when "lower_bound". The `--hunt` document-level `coverage.missed_bytes` reports `eligible_bytes` and `unscanned_fraction` as null: eligibility is each hunter's own, and there is no dump-wide scope to roll up into. `coverage.status`, verdicts, scores, and exit codes are untouched. Report enrichment adds one process-wide `result.summary.process_enrichment` and four card-scoped projections on every triageCardRecord (`exception_context`, `allocation_neighborhood`, `handle_correlation`, `string_context`). Each carries an enrichmentSection stating its scope, missing/partial/complete evidence state, eligible and included counts, cap, truncation, provenance, and limitations. Enrichment is captured evidence only: it never appears in `findings`, `finding_details`, or `verdict`, and it cannot change coverage status or exit behavior. v2.18 adds PE, instruction, and IAT correlation to report enrichment: one process-wide `result.summary.pe_context` (the main image's identity and the main-image correlation layer's consistent/conflict/unavailable tally plus its retained `conflict` observations), and three more card-scoped projections on every triageCardRecord -- `anchor_pe_context` (the anchor placed against the PE image that owns it: headers/code/data/import_iat/relocation/unmapped/outside_image, or private/unresolved when no module owns it, with the section's declared R/W/X versus the live region protection), `instruction_context` (a bounded x86/x64 instruction window at the highest-priority approved anchor source -- an exception RIP, a live thread RIP, a thread StartAddress, then the card anchor -- decoded through an optional isolated disassembler, with direct branch targets and mechanically-proven indirect memory-slot targets resolved to module/section/region), and `iat_correlation` (the anchor module's import table summary plus only the slots a window branch targets or whose live thunk target is unusual). Each carries an enrichmentSection with the same missing/partial/complete semantics. `instruction_context.decoder_state` is `decoded`, `not_run`, `unavailable` (no disassembler installed), `unsupported_arch` (a determined non-x86 machine), `arch_undetermined` (no signal fixed the architecture), `decode_error` (an invalid opcode with room for a whole instruction after it), or `undecoded_tail` (a short trailing run did not decode -- an invalid opcode or a cut-short instruction, indistinguishable); every value but `decoded` makes the section `partial`, as does a window the byte cap or the end of the capture cut short. The decode architecture comes from the COFF `Machine` of the module that owns the chosen anchor, then a WOW64 thread context, then the main image `Machine` (before the host SystemInfo), then the anchor thread's context flavour, then SystemInfo -- so an anchor in unbacked private code is still decoded and a WOW64 process is decoded x86. A `branch_targets` entry with `kind` `indirect_memory` carries `iat_classification_uncertain: true` when the run could not confirm the slot is outside the IAT. A `pe_context` conflict observation, a redirected or private IAT thunk target, and a declared-versus-live protection mismatch are investigation leads, never verdict dimensions: v2.18 changes no `findings`, `finding_details`, `verdict`, `coverage.status`, score, confidence, Finding identity, or exit code.

evidence.description: One entry per evidence source. A single-dump recon command emits exactly one entry (role: 'primary'); a comparison command emits one per side (e.g. 'baseline'/'target').

rules.description: rules.yaml provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.rules_pkg.loader.get_rules_source_info()'s return shape. Omitted entirely (not present as a key at all) when get_rules() was never called this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never reads rules.yaml) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._rules_meta. `path`/`sha256` are only null for the built-in defaults (no file was loaded at all); `path` is basename-only under --redact-paths, matching every other path-bearing meta field's own redaction rule. `version` has no lower bound -- rules_pkg.loader only type-checks a rules.yaml-declared `version:` field, never its sign (see loader.py's own _validate_top_level), so this schema does not invent a constraint the Python side doesn't enforce. `path == null` is EXACTLY the built-in-defaults shape (dumpex.rules_pkg.loader's own hardcoded fallback dict, verified against _load_rules()'s only path==None assignment) -- sha256/explicit/version are pinned to null/false/1 on that branch, not merely nullable.

yara_rules.description: YARA rule-file provenance for this run -- matches dumpex.hunt.yara_hunt.get_yara_provenance()'s return shape. Omitted entirely when YARA scanning was never invoked this run (e.g. --hunt injection alone never loads any .yar/.yara file) -- see dumpex.output.envelope._yara_rules_meta. `rules_dir` is basename-only under --redact-paths. `aggregate_sha256` is never null in this branch -- load_and_compile() always calls hashlib.sha256().hexdigest() unconditionally (even over zero rule files), which never returns null; only the error-only branch below omits it entirely.

hexAddress.description: A memory address/pointer/handle, normalized to a fixed-width (16 hex digit), lowercase, 0x-prefixed string -- or null when there is nothing to report an address for (see dumpex/output/records.py's hex_address()). Never a bare int (uint64 precision isn't safe across all JSON consumers) and never a variable-width string.

module_context.description: resolved: backed by a known module. unregistered: ModuleListStream was available and this address is confirmed NOT backed by any known module (a real DFIR signal). unavailable: ModuleListStream itself is missing -- can't tell either way, must not be confused with 'unregistered'. null: start_address is itself unknown (module context is moot).

sysInfoRecord.description: The 18-field `--sysinfo` record. Process identity and runtime fields belong to `--process`; this record carries system, host, current-directory, and environment facts. `environment_variables` is an ordered array of `{name, value}` entries, never a map, so duplicate names, `=`-prefixed names, and source order remain evidence.

processDiagnosticRecord.description: One `identity_evidence.diagnostics[]` or `iat.diagnostics[]` entry. `code` is a closed seven-value diagnostic vocabulary, distinct from coverage limitations, and `severity` is limited to info or warning. Each code has a closed `details` shape. Recon diagnostics must not contain verdict, confidence, ATT&CK, reconstructed-address, or PEB-authenticity claims.

importEntryRecord.description: One IAT thunk slot. `symbol` is non-null only when `import_by == "name"`; `ordinal` is non-null and decoded from the captured thunk only when `import_by == "ordinal"`.

iatRecord.description: The always-present, non-null `--process` IAT object. `table_present` and `import_directory_present` are three-state values (true, false, or null); the conditions below enforce address, presence, and count consistency. The producer additionally requires `len(entries) == entry_count`, which JSON Schema cannot express.

allOf.description: table_present is not True -> no range to report at all -- table_va/table_size must both be null.
table_va/table_size are always set or unset TOGETHER (parse_iat() never produces one without the other).

import_directory_present is not True -> both null. Deliberately one-directional (unlike table_va/table_size): import_directory_size may legitimately be set while import_directory_va stays null when import_directory_present is True (the declared Size is recorded even when the RVA's own address arithmetic overflowed).

processRecord.description: The single `--process` record, emitted even when every scalar field is null. `identity_evidence` preserves auditable claims from misc-info, PEB, module, and main-image PE sources, including rejected raw values where defined, path-selection provenance, and diagnostics. `peb_extended` is the only optional property in this schema and is present only for `--process --verbose`; all other properties here are required and the object is closed.

peb_extended.description: The seven extended PEB fields, present only for `--process --verbose`. The property is omitted entirely, not set to null, otherwise; it is the only property in this schema outside its object's `required` set.

handleRecord.description: One `--handles` record per HandleDataStream descriptor with a usable handle value. `handle` is a non-null fixed-width hex string. `type_name_status` and `object_name_status` independently distinguish ok, unnamed, and unreadable; each name is non-null exactly when its status is `ok`. `attributes` and `granted_access` remain raw masks.

profileStreamEntry.description: One row of the dump's MINIDUMP_DIRECTORY table. `parser_state` is closed, and the conditions below constrain `record_count` and `detail` for each state. For `parsed`, `record_count` may be an integer for a collection stream or null for a singular stream; JSON Schema cannot distinguish those cases from `stream_type_id` alone.

profileMemoryCapture.description: Explicit memory-capture facts. Do not infer `MiniDumpWithFullMemory` from `Memory64ListStream`; the raw flag and observed memory evidence are independent. `captured_segment_count` and `captured_bytes_total` are either both null or both set.

capabilityLimitation.description: One reason an analysis capability is limited or unavailable. This describes the capability's evidence gap, not whether `--profile` completed. Its `code` vocabulary is closed, unlike the top-level `coverageLimitation.code` vocabulary.

profileCapabilityEntry.description: One row of the closed analysis-capability matrix. Each `required_source_groups` entry is an OR-group with at least one usable source required. `available` has no limitations; `limited` has non-blocking group, optional-source, or truncation limitations; `unavailable` has a blocking required-source limitation and a fully blocked required group. A source may appear in at most one limitation, and `required_sources` is the order-preserving flattened union of the groups.

allOf.description: 'limited' requires at least one limitation, and that limitation set must not include a blocking REQUIRED_SOURCE_* code -- a REQUIRED_SOURCE_* gap makes the capability 'unavailable', never merely 'limited' (mirrors ProfileCapabilityEntry.__post_init__).

'unavailable' requires at least one REQUIRED_SOURCE_* limitation explaining which required evidence is blocking (mirrors ProfileCapabilityEntry.__post_init__'s own 'status is unavailable but carries no REQUIRED_SOURCE_* limitation' rejection).

A multi-member required OR-group is either fully blocked or fully unblocked, never partially (ProfileCapabilityEntry.__post_init__'s own 'blocked_count not in (0, len(group))' rule) -- 'unavailable' requires EVERY member of this capability's own required group to carry its own REQUIRED_SOURCE_* limitation, not just one.

A multi-member required OR-group is either fully blocked or fully unblocked, never partially (ProfileCapabilityEntry.__post_init__'s own 'blocked_count not in (0, len(group))' rule) -- 'unavailable' requires EVERY member of this capability's own required group to carry its own REQUIRED_SOURCE_* limitation, not just one.

profileRecord.description: The `--profile` evidence-capability record. It is emitted exactly once when the dump directory is readable, with complete or partial coverage, and omitted when coverage is `not_evaluated`. `capabilities` contains exactly six fixed capability ids in registry order and never expresses malicious/clean, confidence, ATT&CK, or hunter-score verdicts. The conditions below keep raw flag fields and `memory_capture.full_memory_flag_set` nullable together. The producer also preserves stream directory order and requires each `directory_index` to equal its array position.

capabilities.description: The six fixed capability ids in registry order. Positional constraints prevent repeating, reordering, dropping, or reattributing a capability's source rules.

allOf.description: raw_flags is null iff the header's own trailing union+Flags bytes were themselves truncated (dumpex.commands.profile._decode_flags()) -- nothing was read, so nothing can be recognized/unaccounted, and memory_capture.full_memory_flag_set (read ONLY from raw_flags, per _build_memory_capture()) is equally null.

extractRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ExtractRecord.to_dict() -- the READ-side facts for one --extract invocation. `requested_address`/`requested_size` are never null -- a successful --extract always knows the exact address/size it read (unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, which stay nullable for genuinely optional cases). NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ExtractRecord.__post_init__): bytes_read must never exceed requested_size -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object.

stringRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.StringRecord.to_dict() -- one extracted string from a --strings scan or a --report triage card's own Section 4 (notable_strings). `offset` is a plain byte offset relative to the read region's start, NOT a process address. Unlike most other hexAddress-typed fields in this schema, `address` is never null -- a string was found at some real address, there is no "address unknown" case for it (see StringRecord.__post_init__). `matched_grep` is a flag, not a filter: this record is emitted for every extracted string regardless of --grep -- null when no --grep was given at all (always null for --report's own notable_strings, which has no --grep concept), true/false per record when it was.

stringsSummary.description: The summary for `result.kind == "strings"`. `requested_address` preserves the scan origin even when `data.records` is empty. These six fields are the complete closed summary shape.

reportThreadInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportThreadInfo.to_dict() -- one thread as seen by --report, either the card's own anchor thread (Section 1) or one of the other threads sharing the anchor's resolved region (Section 3). `module_context` is null only when `start_address` is itself null (no address to resolve against). `backing_module_base`/`backing_module_end` are both-or-neither, and only ever non-null when `module_context == 'resolved'` -- Section 3's own 'other threads' entries never populate a range even when resolved (see the class's own docstring).

reportRegionInfo.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportRegionInfo.to_dict() -- the memory region resolved at a triage card's target address (Section 2). `file_offset` is a plain byte offset inside the .dmp file, not a process address, so it does NOT use hexAddress. `module_context`/`mz_header_detected`/`has_injected_pe` are a tri-state triple: `module_context` is never null (a resolved region always has SOME module-context answer); `mz_header_detected` is null iff the small header-peek read itself failed; `has_injected_pe` is null whenever the evidence needed to decide is itself missing (see the class's own docstring for the full derivation table, mirrored in the allOf below).

reportIocString.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportIocString.to_dict() -- one IOC-pattern string hit in a triage card's Section 4. `context_hex`/`context_base_address`/`context_hit_offset` are only ever populated when `is_network_pattern` is true -- a bounded (<=256 byte, i.e. <=512 hex char, enforced via context_hex's own maxLength) collect-time-computed hexdump-context window the renderer decodes instead of re-reading the dump (see dumpex.commands.report.render_report_console's own docstring for why). context_hit_offset's maximum of 255 is the loosest static bound this schema can express (the real constraint -- must fall strictly within THIS instance's own, possibly shorter, context_hex -- compares two sibling field values and is Python-only, see ReportIocString.__post_init__).

enrichmentSection.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.EnrichmentSection.to_dict(). The scope, evidence state, counting, and provenance envelope every report-enrichment projection carries. `total` is the eligible population for the section's own selection class, or null when it is not determinable; `included` is what survived `cap`. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see EnrichmentSection.__post_init__): when `total` is non-null, `truncated` equals `included < total`, `included` never exceeds `total` or `cap`, a `missing` section has total null / included 0 / truncated false, and a `complete` section always has a non-null total.

reportEnvironmentValue.description: One allowlisted environment variable of the dumped process. Only names on the report's own session allowlist appear; the complete environment inventory remains `--sysinfo`. `truncated` says the captured value exceeded the retained-text cap and `value` holds its leading characters.

reportEnvironmentSummary.description: The allowlisted session slice of the process environment block. `entries` always has exactly `section.included` items.

reportHandleTypeCount.description: One type row of the process-wide handle census, using the same display label and bucketing `--handles` itself publishes.

reportHandleSummary.description: The process-wide handle inventory reduced to a bounded per-type census. `total_handles` counts every collected handle independently of how many type rows survived the cap, and is null exactly when the handle stream is missing -- an absent stream counts nothing, it does not count zero.

reportTokenCapability.description: Whether the dump's TokenStream can contribute to this report. `stream_present` is a directory fact and is independent of `parser_state`, which says what dumpex can do with it: a captured stream dumpex has no parser for is stream_present true, parser_state "unparsed", status "unavailable". `parser_state` is non-null exactly when `stream_present` is true.

reportIdentityConflict.description: One disagreement between two captured identity sources, as the canonical process-identity boundary resolved it. A conflict is NOT a coverage gap: both sources were captured and both were read, they simply do not agree. That is why these are separate from the section's `limitations`, which report missing evidence and are what drive its `status` -- a consumer thresholding on `status` must not see a fully captured conflict as a collection gap.

reportProcessEnrichment.description: The one process-wide enrichment of a `--report` run, carried on `result.summary`. Identity comes from the same canonical process-identity boundary `--process` uses, so the two never disagree about one dump. `path_source` names the claim that won the path precedence and requires a non-null `process_path`. Nothing here is a maliciousness judgment. `section.status` is `missing` only when this record publishes no identity claim at all; any resolved pid, path, start time, command line, image base, or module match is evidence that something was evaluated. `process_path` and `command_line` go through the same retained-text cap as every other dump-derived string here and carry their own truncation flags: a PEB string is bounded only by the UNICODE_STRING that carried it. `process_name` is the basename of `process_path`, and a captured path with no separator in it is its own basename, so it is bounded and flagged like the other two. Identity conflicts the process-identity boundary resolved are published in `identity_conflicts`, NOT in `section.limitations`: a conflict leaves the evaluation complete, and only a diagnostic reporting an unavailable preferred source (a path-source fallback) is a completeness fact. `identity_conflicts_total` counts every conflict the boundary reported, including any the cap dropped. Neither ever becomes a finding.

reportAddressContext.description: Where one address published by an exception record actually lives, resolved against the same region table and module list the card itself uses. Every field but `address` is null when no captured region contains it -- an address outside the region table is not a claim that the address is invalid, only that this dump does not describe it. Region facts require a resolved `region_base`.

reportExceptionEntry.description: One retained MINIDUMP_EXCEPTION_STREAM record. `exception_code` is the raw 32-bit code, or null when the captured value is not usable as one -- never a substituted 0x0, which is itself a real code. `exception_code_name` is the parser's own decoded name, or null for a code it does not recognize. `parameters` are published positionally, with an unusable element rendered `0x?` in place rather than dropped: position carries meaning, and dropping one would relabel every following value. For an access violation or in-page error, `access_type` and `referenced_address` are that positional decode, and `address_context`/`referenced_context` resolve the faulting and referenced addresses against the card's own region and module views. `selection_reason` says only how the record relates to this card's anchor -- an exception is execution state, never in itself a maliciousness observation.

reportExceptionContext.description: One card's bounded view of the dump's ExceptionStream. `entries` always has exactly `section.included` items and is deduplicated by `index`. Address resolution is only as complete as the region view behind it: when that view dropped a descriptor AND an address here resolved to no captured region, the section reports `partial` rather than claiming the address lies outside every captured region.

reportNeighborRegion.description: One region of the anchor's allocation neighborhood. `distance` is the byte gap to the anchor region and is 0 for the anchor itself and for an immediately adjacent region. Adjacency is memory layout, not a relationship to the anchor. `module_owner` is the loaded module whose range holds this region's base, or null for an unregistered mapping and for a dump with no module list to resolve against.

reportAllocationNeighborhood.description: One card's bounded region layout around its anchor. `entries` always has exactly `section.included` items, in ascending base-address order and deduplicated by base address (Python-only: JSON Schema cannot compare sibling array items). A region descriptor the region model cannot represent is absent from the table this section describes, so `section.status` is `partial` and a limitation names how many were dropped. A `missing` section distinguishes a MemoryInfoListStream that was never collected from one the dump declares but no parsed stream is available for, and from one that failed to parse: its `limitations` name which.

reportCorrelatedHandle.description: One handle whose named kernel object also appears in the text this card examined. The match is on the object name's LAST path segment only: a namespace prefix (Device, BaseNamedObjects, REGISTRY) is shared by thousands of unrelated objects, so matching on any segment would correlate unrelated objects and fill the retained subset with noise. The correlation is textual -- two independent captures of the same name in one dump -- and is not proof that the anchor uses the handle. The complete inventory remains `--handles`. `attributes`, `handle_count`, and `pointer_count` are the raw, undecoded descriptor fields, carried so a correlated handle can be assessed without a second `--handles` run. `object_name_truncated` says the captured name exceeded the retained-text cap: the match is made against the WHOLE captured name, so a truncated value can lack the segment that selected it. Every dump-derived string here -- object name and type name alike -- obeys the same retained-text cap and carries its own truncation flag.

reportHandleCorrelation.description: One card's bounded, deduplicated subset of the process-wide handle inventory. `entries` always has exactly `section.included` items and is deduplicated by `handle`, which is a record's whole identity: a malformed dump that declares one handle value twice yields one entry. This section rests on two bodies of evidence and is `complete` only when both are: `section.status` is `partial` when the handle summary is partial, when a handle's object name could not be read, or when the card's own region read came up short -- in each case a non-match may be a non-read rather than an absence.

reportStringContextEntry.description: One string retained as navigation context for a card's anchor. `distance` is the absolute byte distance from `reportStringContext.distance_anchor_address` and is null exactly for the `query_match` entry, which is itself the anchor. Proximity is layout: an adjacent string is not claimed to be referenced or executed by anything at the anchor.

reportStringContext.description: The anchor-aware, bounded string projection of one card's own content scan. Every entry is selected out of the strings that single content read already produced -- no region is read or scanned a second time. NOT expressed here (Python-only): each entry's `address` equals `examined_base_address` plus its own `offset`, each `offset` falls inside `bytes_read`, at most one entry is a `query_match`, and `entries` has exactly `section.included` items. `query_text` is the needle that was searched for, kept apart from the `query_match` entry's own `text`, which is the string actually captured at the hit; an embedded needle means the two differ. One captured string yields at most one entry: the string enclosing the hit is published as the `query_match` entry and is never re-emitted as adjacent context. NOT expressed here (Python-only): a `query_match` entry requires a non-null `query_text`, and no two entries share an `offset`.

reportPeObservation.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportPeObservation.to_dict(). One dumpex.core.pe_correlation.Observation reduced to a wire record. `state` is the three-valued correlation result; `reason` the dumpex-authored token behind it; `sources` names the evidence evaluated; `operands` the exact scalar values compared. A `conflict` is a disagreement between two captured facts, never a maliciousness finding. Only `conflict` observations are retained in reportPeContext.observations.

reportPeContext.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportPeContext.to_dict(). The one process-wide PE projection of a --report run: the main image's identity (the canonical PeImageProfile's own decoded values) and the main-image correlation layer's tally and retained conflicts. `consistent_count`/`conflict_count`/`unavailable_count` tally every observation the correlation produced; `observations` carries only the retained conflicts. NOT expressed here (Python-only): when `section.total` is non-null it equals `conflict_count`, `observations` has exactly `section.included` items, and every retained observation has state `conflict`.

reportAnchorPeContext.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportAnchorPeContext.to_dict(). This card's anchor placed against the PE image that owns it. `classification` is headers/code/data/import_iat/relocation/unmapped/outside_image, `module` when the owning module's profile was unavailable to place it finer, or private/unresolved when no module owns it. `protection_matches_declared` compares the section's own R/W/X bits with the live region protection -- an observation an analyst follows up, never a verdict. NOT expressed here (Python-only): a `*_truncated` flag requires its value present.

reportDecodedInstruction.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportDecodedInstruction.to_dict(). One decoded instruction of the card's bounded window. `text` is the capstone mnemonic and operands, cut to the retained-text cap. `branch_kind` is the mechanically determinable shape of the branch operand.

reportBranchTarget.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportBranchTarget.to_dict(). One resolved branch target from the card's instruction window. `target_address` is the direct destination for a `direct` target and the memory slot address for `iat_slot`/`indirect_memory`; `resolved_target_address` is the pointer read from that slot. An `indirect_register` target resolves no address -- the destination is run-time state. `iat_classification_uncertain` is set only on an `indirect_memory` target the run could not confirm is outside the IAT (the owning module's IAT directory bounds were unreadable and no import table parsed). NOT expressed here (Python-only): an `indirect_register` target carries no addresses, a `direct` target carries no `resolved_target_address`, `iat_symbol` is only set for an `iat_slot` target, and `iat_classification_uncertain` is only set for an `indirect_memory` target.

reportInstructionContext.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportInstructionContext.to_dict(). The card's bounded instruction window and its resolved branch targets. `anchor_source` names which approved anchor the window was read at, in priority order: an exception RIP, a live thread RIP, a thread StartAddress, then the card anchor (an explicit --report-addr leads). `decoder_state` is `decoded`, `not_run` (no captured bytes), `unavailable` (no disassembler installed), `unsupported_arch`, `arch_undetermined`, `decode_error`, or `undecoded_tail` (a short trailing run did not decode -- an invalid opcode or a cut-short instruction, indistinguishable); every value but `decoded` makes the section `partial`. Nothing here names a function, an argument, or a call stack. NOT expressed here (Python-only): `instructions` has exactly `section.included` items, `branch_targets` has at most `branch_targets_total`, and `branch_targets_truncated` equals `len(branch_targets) < branch_targets_total`.

reportIatCorrelatedEntry.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportIatCorrelatedEntry.to_dict(). One IAT slot retained for this card: instruction-correlated, or with a live thunk target unusual enough to be an investigation lead. `iat_slot_va` is the slot's own address; `resolved_target_va` is the pointer currently in it. `selection_reason` is the primary reason; `also_selected_for` lists any additional reasons. A private, unregistered, or redirected target is a lead, never a verdict dimension.

reportIatCorrelation.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ReportIatCorrelation.to_dict(). This card's bounded view of the anchor module's import address table: the module summary, plus only the slots a window branch targets or whose live thunk target is unusual. An anchor in no module, or a module with no import directory, leaves this `missing` (no owning module) or `complete` with an empty subset (no imports). NOT expressed here (Python-only): `entries` has exactly `section.included` items and is deduplicated by `iat_slot_va`.

triageCardRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.TriageCardRecord.to_dict() -- one --report triage card. --report-string produces N cards (one per private-memory hit region) in one result.data.records list; --report-tid/--report-addr produce exactly one. `findings` is a closed, deduplicated vocabulary; `verdict` is cross-checked against len(findings) via the allOf below (0/1/2/3+ -> CLEAN/SUSPICIOUS/LIKELY_MALICIOUS/HIGH_CONFIDENCE_MALICIOUS), the same four-tier rule dumpex.core.memory.verdict_for() enforces in Python. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see TriageCardRecord.__post_init__): string_scan['truncated'] must equal bytes_read < requested_bytes, and findings/finding_details must name exactly the same keys -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES against each other within one object. `exception_context`, `allocation_neighborhood`, `handle_correlation`, `string_context`, `anchor_pe_context`, `instruction_context`, and `iat_correlation` are the card-scoped enrichment projections; each is bounded, carries its own enrichmentSection, and is captured evidence only -- none of them appears in `findings`, `finding_details`, or `verdict`, and none can change coverage status or the exit code. NOT expressed here (Python-only): `string_context.anchor_address` and `anchor_pe_context.anchor_address` equal this card's own `anchor_address`.

reportSummary.description: The summary for `result.kind == "report"`. `mode` identifies --report-tid, --report-addr, --report-string, or the tid-plus-address combination; the conditions below require the corresponding non-null query fields. `skipped_unreadable_regions`, `truncated_regions`, and `clamped_regions` are string-search counters and remain zero outside string-search mode. `process_enrichment` is the one process-wide enrichment of the run, shared by every card in it rather than repeated per card. `cards_skipped_for_budget` counts actionable hit regions this invocation did not triage because it reached its own card/read budget. The hit counters keep naming everything the search found, so a skipped hit is never folded away: Every hit is classified, grouped, budgeted and carded against the region that COVERS its address, not the region the search read it from; on an overlapping region table those differ, so `hits_private`/`hits_image`/`image_hit_modules` describe the same regions the cards do. `hits_sharing_a_region` counts hits inside a region another hit is already carded for -- only groups that actually received a card, since a group the budget skipped covers nothing. `cards_skipped_for_budget` counts those skipped regions and `hits_skipped_for_budget` the hits inside them, which are unanalyzed rather than represented elsewhere. `card_count` plus `hits_sharing_a_region` plus `hits_skipped_for_budget` accounts for `hits_private`, and `hits_private` plus `hits_image` accounts for `total_hits`. A budget stop additionally reports `execution_status: partial`. `pe_context` is the one process-wide PE projection of the run -- the main image's identity and the main-image correlation layer's tally and retained conflicts -- shared by every card. These seventeen fields are the complete closed summary shape.

moduleDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ModuleDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/rebased module between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_modules' own set logic. `name` is always a non-empty string ("(unnamed)" for an anonymous module -- see dumpex.commands.comparison._module_display_name), but full_path_before/full_path_after are only forced null on the side that genuinely has no entry -- the PRESENT side's full_path may legitimately be null too (an anonymous module has a real base_address but no name at all), so only base_address is required non-null for added/removed. `full_path_before`/`full_path_after` are otherwise unconstrained by change_type: address identifies a module diff, not path. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see ModuleDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "rebased"`, base_address_before must differ from base_address_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

threadDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ThreadDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed thread between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_threads' own TID-keyed set logic. backing_module_after/backing_module_context are only ever populated for 'added' (resolved against the TARGET's module list); diff_threads never attempts baseline-side module resolution for a removed thread. For 'added': backing_module_after/backing_module_context are both null exactly when start_address_after itself is null (module resolution is never attempted without a known address); otherwise backing_module_context is always one of resolved/unregistered/unavailable, and backing_module_after is non-null iff backing_module_context is 'resolved'.

memoryDiffRecord.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.MemoryDiffRecord.to_dict() -- one added/removed/protection-changed memory region between two dumps, grounded in dumpex.commands.diff.diff_memory's own BaseAddress-keyed set logic. suspicious_before/_after reuse memoryRegionRecord.suspicious's own semantics rather than diff_memory's own 4-tier console categorization. NOT expressed here (Python-only, see MemoryDiffRecord.__post_init__): for `change_type: "protection_changed"`, protect_before must differ from protect_after -- JSON Schema cannot compare two sibling field VALUES for inequality within one object.

comparisonRecord.description: Tagged union for result.kind == 'comparison' -- discriminated by entity_type, which is a distinct const on each branch.

kind.description: Selects the canonical record type held by `result.data.records`; this is a closed vocabulary.

execution_status.description: Did the COMMAND itself run to completion -- independent of whether the EVIDENCE it saw was complete (see coverage below). 'partial' is used by --report when a self-imposed scan-budget clamp (MAX_REGION_READ) or a per-card --output write failure means the command didn't finish everything it set out to do, even though the evidence it DID look at may be fully covered.

status.description: Was the evidence available to this command complete? Vocabulary shared with dumpex.hunt._coverage.derive_coverage_status.

reasons.description: Backward-compatible flat human text, rendered from `limitations` -- kept so an existing consumer that only reads `reasons` never breaks.

sources.description: Per-source observed state -- keyed by source name (e.g. 'memory_info', 'threads', or a dotted entity-namespaced name such as 'baseline.modules' for a comparison result). Optional: an older producer that doesn't populate this is still a valid document.

limitations.description: Structured, machine-readable coverage gaps from which `reasons` is rendered. `code` intentionally remains an open string vocabulary so new limitation codes do not require a schema-version change.

summary.description: Free-form per-kind extension point by default (open object) -- refined per-kind via the allOf/if-then block below exactly like data.records is, wherever a kind's own summary fields carry machine-relevant facts (e.g. kind == 'strings'/'report', whose requested_address/query_* fields are the only way to know a zero-result scan's own origin).

diagnosticEntry.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.Diagnostic.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `code` is required (it's always a key in the dict), just nullable.

sourceObservation.description: Matches dumpex.output.coverage.SourceObservation.to_dict(), which always emits all three fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just `state`, and the record_count<->state invariant (None for absent/failed, exactly 0 for present_empty, >=1 for present) is frozen structurally below, mirroring the same invariant SourceObservation.__post_init__ enforces in Python.

scanTarget.description: One memory region or segment a scan did not examine, attached to a coverage limitation so the unresolved virtual range is explicit. `size_limit` is non-null only for an oversized skip and records the cap exceeded; the owning limitation's `scope` names the scan layer. `file_offset` is a dump-file byte offset and is null when the bytes were not captured. MemoryInfo fields are null for `kind == "memory_segment"`. `captured_size` and `capture_state` describe dump capture independently of a hunter's read attempt: state is null when size is unknown, none at zero, complete when equal to `size`, and partial otherwise. The producer additionally requires non-null `size_limit < size` and `captured_size <= size`, comparisons JSON Schema cannot express. `examined_size` is how many of `captured_size` bytes the scan that recorded this gap actually examined -- 0 for a target nothing read, the returned length for a short read, a stop cursor for a scan a budget ended partway through -- and null when that extent was never established. `unexamined_size` is `captured_size - examined_size`, null whenever either side is, and 0 whenever `captured_size` is 0 (a target the dump holds no bytes for missed none; what it needs is a re-collection, which `capture_state` already says). Null is not 0: an unestablished extent is what makes a gap unquantifiable, and the producer unions only the non-null ones into `coverage.missed_bytes`. The producer additionally requires `examined_size <= captured_size` and refuses `examined_size` without a `captured_size` to measure it against.

allOf.description: capture_state is derived from captured_size -- null iff captured_size is null.

coverageLimitation.description: A coverage gap record that always emits every field, using null or `[]` where a code does not use one. The conditions below constrain known codes, fixed sources, allowed defaults, dependencies, and source-specific oversized-target kinds. Unknown `code` or `source` values remain open. Producer-only checks compare sibling values or external source state, including source inequality, counterpart record counts, `affected_count == len(targets)`, and other relationships JSON Schema cannot express. v2.14 adds `TARGETED_SOURCE_NOT_EVALUATED`, emitted only by targeted (`--hunt-addr`) hunt records. Sourced to `targeted_scan` it means one granted coverage closure did not run, with `scope` naming that closure; sourced to any other name it means that coverage source is outside what a targeted invocation of the analyzer evaluates at all, and it legitimately accompanies a `complete` coverage status.

targets.description: Typed region or segment references identifying what a scan did not examine. Codes that do not use targets emit `[]`. SCAN_REGION_OVERSIZED_SKIPPED requires a non-empty array; the read-failed, short-read, scan-truncated, and scan-not-started codes may use `[]` when target identity is unavailable. Whenever targets are present, the producer requires their count to equal `affected_count`.

budget_limit.description: The configured limit for the resource budget named by `scope`; `budget_consumed` records the observed use. This structured value is independent of free-text `detail`. Minimum 0 permits a deliberately disabled budget. Non-null only with a non-null `scope`.

budget_consumed.description: The REAL amount of the resource actually consumed at the moment the budget was attributed, when set -- NOT assumed to equal budget_limit: it can exceed the limit (a counter incremented, or elapsed time measured, only after the check that stops the scan) or sit under it (a predictive check that stops the scan just before an action that would exceed the limit). Minimum 0, same reasoning as budget_limit.

allOf.description: Read-failed, short-read, scan-truncated, and scan-not-started targets are not oversized skips, so their `size_limit` must be null.

PE_HEADER_SCAN_TRUNCATED and PE_HEADER_SCAN_NOT_STARTED may name the stopping hidden-PE budget in `scope` (reads_per_region, total_bytes, validations_per_region, or validations_total) with its limit and consumption. All three fields are null when no budget stopped the scan; the producer requires them to be set or null together.

YARA_HIT_CAP_REACHED and YARA_SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED may identify the stopping YARA budget in `scope` (max_total_hits, scan_deadline_seconds, or max_total_bytes_scanned) with its limit and consumption.

CS_BEACON_SCAN_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED may identify the stopping budget in `scope` (scan_deadline_seconds, max_total_scanned_bytes, max_candidates, max_decoded_bytes, or max_hits) with its limit and consumption. `detail` remains a separate human-readable reason.
All other codes leave `budget_limit` and `budget_consumed` null. This branch does not constrain `scope`, which has separate meanings for other coverage codes.

missedBytes.description: How much captured in-scope memory a run's coverage gaps add up to. `bytes` is a total only when `state` is "exact"; it is a floor when "lower_bound" and null when "unknown". It measures memory, not gap records: the producer unions the unexamined address ranges, so one physical region reported by several gaps at once is counted once and the figure can never exceed what the dump captured. `quantified_gaps` counts gap records whose extent is established, `distinct_ranges` the merged ranges those cover. A `complete` coverage status always reports state "exact" with 0 bytes and no gaps, and a `partial` whose reasons cost no capturable bytes reports the same thing -- a gap is never invented to match a status. The producer additionally requires `distinct_ranges <= quantified_gaps`, the one relationship JSON Schema cannot express. The three states are decided by the two gap counts alone: "exact" when `unquantified_gaps` is 0, "lower_bound" when both counts are non-zero, and "unknown" when only `unquantified_gaps` is. `eligible_bytes` is the captured bytes each scan pass had in front of it, summed over the passes and including anything a pass never reached, and `unscanned_pass_bytes` is the same quantity for the gaps -- unioned within a pass, summed across them. `unscanned_fraction` is `unscanned_pass_bytes / eligible_bytes` and carries `state`'s qualifier: exact when "exact", a floor when "lower_bound". These three share a per-pass basis that `bytes` does not: `bytes` unions the same gaps into MEMORY, so a region three passes each skipped is one region of `bytes` and three passes' worth of `unscanned_pass_bytes`, and the two are published side by side rather than divided into each other. `eligible_bytes` and `unscanned_fraction` are null when no denominator was established (including every not_evaluated coverage status, and any scan loop that took items into scope without measuring them); `unscanned_fraction` is null when `state` is "unknown" or `eligible_bytes` is 0 as well, since 0 means the run missed nothing and must not stand in for an unmeasured gap.

artifact.description: An output file the tool itself produced (e.g. an extracted memory region) -- distinct from meta.evidence, which describes the INPUT dump(s). Populated by --extract and --report (its own optional extract-to-file side effect, under a different `kind` string -- 'extracted_region' vs 'report_extracted_region'). Matches dumpex.output.records.Artifact.to_dict(), which always emits all six fields -- `required` covers all of them, not just id/kind/path.

finding.description: One hunter-agnostic judgment in a hunter record's `findings` array, combining facts, inference, confidence, rationale, limitations, normalized identity, severity, ATT&CK mappings, evidence references, IOCs, and rule provenance. `id` is a deterministic 128-bit SHA-256 prefix for the same finding content, not a globally unique cross-dump identifier; combine it with `meta.evidence[].sha256`. `severity` is derived from tag and confidence. `technique_ids` must be real mapped techniques and may be empty. `rule_version` is null unless a versioned rule source produced the finding; rules.yaml findings use its content hash, not its format-version field. YARA records keep matches in `YaraDetails` and require `findings == []`.

id.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._finding.Finding's own "finding-" + 32 lowercase hex chars (128-bit SHA-256 prefix) shape exactly -- pattern PLUS an exact minLength/maxLength, same reasoning as technique_ids' own two-branch shape above (a bare '^...$' pattern alone would accept a trailing-newline-appended value one character too long).

items.description: A MITRE ATT&CK technique (`T1055`) or sub-technique (`T1559.001`) id. Each branch combines a pattern with an exact length because `$` may also match before a trailing newline; the length bound rejects that case without a non-standard anchor.

allOf.description: `severity` is a pure function of `(tag, confidence)`. This condition pins the nine-value mapping so every producer must keep severity consistent with those fields.

huntRegionRef.description: A reproducible memory-region reference inside a hunter's `details`. `base_address` is never null because every region reference names a real address.

huntThreadRef.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRef.to_dict() -- a TID plus optional StartAddress/current-instruction-pointer, hex-formatted. `ip`/`ip_reg` are both-or-neither: a thread reference either carries no live register snapshot (both null) or a real one (both set) -- there is no case where the register name is known but its value isn't, or vice versa.

huntThreadRegionHit.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HuntThreadRegionHit.to_dict() -- a thread correlated with a specific region, e.g. a thread's current RIP/EIP executing inside a flagged allocation, or its StartAddress falling inside one.

huntPeHeaderHit.description: One MZ candidate examined for a hidden PE header, including its exact location, containing region, and structural-validation outcome. `entry_point_rva` is an integer RVA; the header's declared `image_base` is a hex address. `reason` is set only when `valid` is false, while PE fact fields are set only when it is true. `va` is the candidate address, `region_offset` its offset inside `region`, and `file_offset` its dump-file offset or null when uncaptured. At a region base, `va == region.base_address` and `region_offset == 0`.

injectionDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.InjectionDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt injection`'s hunter-specific evidence. `pe_read_failed`/`pe_short_reads` deliberately do NOT appear here -- those are coverage counts, not evidence (see PE_HEADER_READ_FAILED/PE_HEADER_SHORT_READ limitations under this hunter's own coverage instead).

hollowingDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.HollowingDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt hollowing`'s hunter-specific evidence: the four checks (memory type / MZ header / RWX protection at the image base, and the PEB-vs-module-list name compare). Unlike the other six hunters, every field here is a scalar -- all fields are scalar. `image_base` is null exactly when the PEB itself is missing (this hunter's NOT_EVALUATED case) -- there is no image base to report at all, unlike every other hunter's details, which always have SOME evidence even under incomplete coverage.

stompingDetails.description: The `--hunt stomping` evidence. `protection_leads` and `verified_changes` entries are intentionally schema-open objects because the collector does not enforce a narrower entry shape. `targeted_scope` is present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan.

targeted_scope.description: Present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan, with one entry per coverage closure in the analyzer's own fixed closure order. A full-scope result omits the key entirely rather than emitting null.

pipeDetails.description: The `--hunt pipe` evidence. Entries are intentionally schema-open objects because the collector does not enforce a narrower entry shape. `targeted_scope` is present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan.

targeted_scope.description: Present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan, with one entry per coverage closure in the analyzer's own fixed closure order. A full-scope result omits the key entirely rather than emitting null.

csBeaconDetails.description: The `--hunt cs-beacon` evidence. The producer requires `config_count == len(configs)`, which JSON Schema cannot compare. Each config's `fields` object is keyed by field name (`BeaconType` or `field_0xNNNN` for an unknown id), and each value contains only `type` and `value`; numeric-only keys and a nested `name` property are rejected. Other config-item properties remain schema-open. `targeted_scope` is present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan.

fields.description: Keyed by field name; `propertyNames` rejects purely numeric keys.

targeted_scope.description: Present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan, with one entry per coverage closure in the analyzer's own fixed closure order. A full-scope result omits the key entirely rather than emitting null.

yaraDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.YaraDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt yara`'s hunter-specific evidence. Deliberately off the shared `finding` model -- a YARA rule hit is a structural pattern match, not a check/facts/inference/confidence/rationale judgment. `targeted_scope` is present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan.

targeted_scope.description: Present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan, with one entry per coverage closure in the analyzer's own fixed closure order. A full-scope result omits the key entirely rather than emitting null.

obfuscationDetails.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.ObfuscationDetails.to_dict() -- `--hunt obfuscation`'s hunter-specific evidence: the seven decode layers' own hit lists. `targeted_scope` is present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan.

targeted_scope.description: Present only for a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan, with one entry per coverage closure in the analyzer's own fixed closure order. A full-scope result omits the key entirely rather than emitting null.

targetedScope.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.TargetedScopeRecord.to_dict() -- one coverage closure of a targeted (`--hunt-addr`) rescan. `base_address`/`size` are always the REQUESTED range, never the containing descriptor and never the captured prefix, so a closure's identity is (hunter, source, scope, base_address, size) whatever the capture outcome was. Capture and evaluation are independent: `captured_size`/`capture_state` describe byte availability in the dump, while `coverage_status` describes how far that source's own algorithm got. A complete capture can still evaluate partially (a retained budget), and a partial capture can be not_evaluated (the bytes never reached the algorithm's minimum input). `coverage_status` "not_applicable" is a fourth, distinct outcome: the source's own descriptor-eligibility gate declined this target, so nothing here was missed and no re-collection, larger budget, or narrower request would change it -- `applicability_reason` names the gate, and the record's `coverage.status` reduction leaves such a closure out rather than letting it turn a completed sibling into a coverage failure. `measurements` is what the closure retained about work it completed without a hit; the entries are observations only and never imply a finding, a score, or coverage of any other source. `scope` is the closure scope (a layer name) and null for an unscoped source. Producer-only: `coverage_status` "complete" requires `capture_state` "complete", `captured_size` never exceeds `size`, and `applicability_reason` is non-null exactly when `coverage_status` is "not_applicable".

applicability_reason.description: The descriptor-eligibility gate that declined this target, from a closed set; null for every `coverage_status` other than "not_applicable".

measurements.description: Neutral measurements this closure retained -- bytes evaluated, values measured, bounds reached -- so a completed no-hit closure still records what it did. Observations only. `name` is not unique within a closure: a bounded top-N list is N entries sharing one name, in the order the closure ranked them.

hunterRecord.description: One hunter's complete entry in `result.data.records` for `result.kind == "hunt"`. `hunter` selects one of seven details shapes. `max_score`, `confidence`, `lead_count`, and `review_priority` are all null for YARA and otherwise must not be partially populated. `coverage` belongs to this hunter; top-level `result.coverage` combines selected hunters. In v2.14 a TARGETED hunter record (one whose `details` carries `targeted_scope`) relaxes one relationship every earlier version held: `coverage.status` may be "complete" while `coverage.limitations` is non-empty. A targeted rescan's status answers "was the requested range fully evaluated for the granted source", while its `TARGETED_SOURCE_NOT_EVALUATED` limitations name the analyzer's other coverage sources that a targeted invocation never evaluates -- the boundary of what the result is about, not a gap in what it did. A consumer must therefore not read a non-empty `limitations` array as "this result has a gap" without checking the code. Full-scope records are unchanged: for them `complete` still implies an empty `limitations`.

huntSummary.description: The shared cross-hunter summary for `result.kind == "hunt"`. `selected` is `all` or one hunter name. When any hunter is DETECTED, `highest_verdict_level` is chosen only from detected hunters; otherwise it is the strongest clean, inconclusive, or not-evaluated signal. `scan_scope` names what the invocation covered: a whole-dump hunt, or one `--hunt-addr` targeted rescan. A targeted invocation always names exactly one analyzer, so its `selected` is never "all".

scan_scope.description: What this hunt invocation actually covered, as a closed tagged shape. `kind` "full" is a whole-dump hunt and carries nothing else; `kind` "targeted" is a single-range `--hunt-addr` rescan and carries the analyzer, the one granted coverage source it ran, the scopes its coverage closures were attributed under, and the normalized requested range. `scopes` is the sorted set of scopes appearing in that result's `details.targeted_scope`, so the two always agree: it is empty only when the invocation's closures carry no scope at all, and is NOT the analyzer's granted scope set (pipe's grant is unscoped while its invocation closes `pipe_name` and `c2_context` independently). Present in both modes, so scope is never inferred from the absence of a field.

skipRelationship.description: One `(hunter, source, scope, cause)` relationship explaining why this physical target was skipped. `source` and `scope` mirror the owning coverage limitation, with `source` remaining open. `cause` distinguishes oversized, read-failed, short-read, scan-truncated, and scan-not-started gaps. `size_limit` is non-null only for `oversized_skipped` and is null for I/O and budget failures.

budget_kind.description: The independent scan budget that caused scan_truncated, scan_not_started, hit_cap_reached, or scan_budget_exhausted. Allowed names are scoped to the injection, YARA, and Cobalt Strike scanners. Null for every other cause.

budget_limit.description: That budget's own configured limit, or null when budget_kind is null. Minimum 0 (not 1) -- a configured budget of exactly 0 is legal (e.g. "no validations at all").

budget_consumed.description: The REAL amount of the resource actually consumed at the moment the budget was attributed, when set -- NOT assumed to equal budget_limit: it can exceed the limit (a counter incremented, or elapsed time measured, only after the check that stops the scan) or sit under it (a predictive check that stops the scan just before an action that would exceed the limit). Minimum 0, same reasoning as budget_limit.

allOf.description: `budget_kind`, `budget_limit`, and `budget_consumed` are set together only for budget-related injection, YARA, or Cobalt Strike causes; every other cause leaves all three null.

contentFinding.description: One structured finding from opt-in `--triage-skipped` deep reading, backing `triage.content_reason_codes`. `type` selects two closed, mutually exclusive shapes: `ioc_string` sets offset, encoding, value, and network-pattern state while leaving module context null; `mz_header` sets module context and leaves string-only fields null. Values are bounded and at most 20 findings accompany an action, so this is an investigative lead rather than complete content or an extractable artifact.

triageInfo.description: Triage state for one investigation action. Metadata mode performs no content read and therefore fixes status to completed with zero bytes, false `region_fully_examined`, empty reason/finding arrays, zero count, and no truncation. Deep mode is opt-in and budgeted: not_captured, budget_deferred, and unreadable mean no successful read and no content signal; completed means at least one byte and the full target examined; partial and clamped mean at least one byte but incomplete examination, caused respectively by missing captured bytes or triage policy limits. Content reason codes and findings occur only after a successful read and are bounded evidence, not verdicts or proof that the originating coverage gap is resolved. Findings are selected representative-first so each reason can retain backing evidence. `finding_count` is the total before selection, and `findings_truncated` is true exactly when it exceeds `len(findings)`. MZ_HEADER_DETECTED is the raw header signal; INJECTED_PE_HEADER additionally requires confirmed unregistered memory, so unavailable module classification cannot produce that stronger claim.

recommendedAction.description: Matches dumpex.hunt._investigation.RecommendedAction.to_dict(). `hunters` is present only on type == "targeted_hunter_rescan".

investigationAction.description: One deduplicated physical skipped target with all contributing hunter, source, scope, and cause relationships merged into `skipped_by`. `priority` and `evidence_availability` are independent: missing captured bytes can require recollection without increasing suspicion. `coverage_effect` is fixed to `original_hunter_gap_not_resolved`; triage does not claim a targeted hunter rescan occurred.

targetedMeasurement.description: Matches dumpex.output.records.TargetedMeasurement.to_dict() -- one thing a targeted closure measured. `value` is null only when the closure genuinely did not measure this quantity; its type follows `unit` (bool for "flag", a non-empty string for "text", a non-negative number otherwise). `base_address`/`size` locate the measurement inside the requested range when it has a location (an entropy window) and are null for a measurement about the closure as a whole; `size` is never set without `base_address`.
